title: Algorithmic Fairness in NLP: Persona-Infused LLMs for Human-Centric Hate Speech Detection
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the performance of Persona-Infused LLMs in detecting hate speech targeting specific social groups, including religious groups. It measures how adopting an in-group persona (matching the target's identity) versus an out-group persona affects detection accuracy (F1 score), false positive rates (FPR), and false negative rates (FNR). Specifically for religion, it compares Muslim and Jewish personas (in-group) against Catholic personas (out-group) when detecting hate speech against Muslims and Jews.
findings: The study found that LLM annotators adopting an in-group persona generally achieved higher F1 scores in detecting hate speech targeting their group compared to out-group personas. Specifically, for hate speech targeting Muslims, the Muslim persona outperformed the Catholic out-group persona in most settings (e.g., Gemini F1 0.648 vs 0.635 with shallow prompting). Similarly, for hate speech targeting Jewish individuals, the Jewish persona often outperformed the Catholic persona (e.g., Gemini Deep Context F1 0.650 vs 0.602). Deeply contextualized personas further improved detection accuracy over shallow personas.
